It also allows women to work at night with their consent and subject to safety conditions, and requires welfare facilities such as canteens and safety committees above specified worker thresholds.

The Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970 is now subsumed in the OSH Code, 2020, which applies its contract labour provisions to establishments and contractors engaging 50 or more contract workers (up from 20 under the old Act). Contractors need a single, all-India licence valid for five years, and the principal employer remains responsible for wages and welfare facilities if the contractor defaults. The Code prohibits contract labour in core activities, with exceptions such as where the normal practice is to use contractors or the work is intermittent, so a factory may outsource canteen and security but generally not its main production line.

The Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 has not been merged into the Labour Codes and continues to apply. It prohibits employment of children below 14 in any occupation, except helping in a family enterprise outside school hours in non-hazardous work or working as a child artist, and bars adolescents aged 14 to 18 from hazardous occupations and processes listed in the Schedule. Employing a child is punishable with imprisonment of six months to two years and/or fine of ₹20,000 to ₹50,000, and repeat offences carry imprisonment of one to three years.

quiz.q: A unit uses power and employs 15 workers. Under the OSH Code, 2020 is it a 'factory'?
options: Yes, all units using power are factories
No, the threshold with power is 20 workers
No, the threshold is 40 workers in all cases
quiz.explain: The OSH Code defines a factory as premises with 20 or more workers using power, or 40 or more without power.

quiz.q: A worker works 10 hours on a day in a factory where the normal day is 8 hours. How is he paid for the extra 2 hours?
options: At twice the ordinary rate of wages
quiz.explain: The OSH Code requires overtime work to be paid at twice the ordinary rate of wages.

quiz.q: A contractor supplies 35 workers to a company. Is a contractor licence needed under the OSH Code?
options: Yes, licence is needed for 20 or more workers
Yes, every contractor needs a licence
No, the threshold under the Code is 50 contract workers
Only if workers are inter-state migrants
quiz.explain: The OSH Code raised the applicability threshold for contract labour provisions from 20 to 50 workers.

quiz.q: A contractor fails to pay wages to contract workers engaged in a factory. Who must pay?
options: Nobody; workers must sue the contractor
The principal employer, who can recover from the contractor
quiz.explain: Under the OSH Code, the principal employer must pay unpaid wages of contract labour and may recover them from the contractor.

quiz.q: A 12-year-old helps in her family's tailoring shop for two hours after school. The position under the 1986 Act is:
options: Permitted, as helping a family enterprise in non-hazardous work outside school hours is excepted
quiz.explain: Section 3 of the Child and Adolescent Labour Act allows a child to help the family enterprise in non-hazardous work after school hours.

quiz.q: A 16-year-old is employed in a mine. This is:
options: Prohibited, as mines are hazardous occupations for adolescents
Permitted if hours are limited to 6
quiz.explain: The 1986 Act prohibits employment of adolescents (14-18) in hazardous occupations, which include mines.

desc.q: A garment exporter with 180 workers on its rolls and 60 contract workers supplied by a contractor wants women to work night shifts and plans to outsource stitching (its core activity) to the contractor. Advise under the applicable law.
points: The unit is a factory under the OSH Code, 2020 (replacing the Factories Act, 1948) and needs a single registration and licence; hours are capped at 8 a day and 48 a week with double-rate overtime.
Women can work night shifts (beyond 7 pm or before 6 am) only with their consent and subject to safety, holiday and transport conditions the appropriate government sets.
With 50 or more contract workers, the OSH Code's contract labour provisions (replacing the CLRA Act, 1970) apply, and the contractor needs a licence.

Contract labour is prohibited in core activities like stitching unless an exception applies (such as normal practice in the industry or work not requiring full-time workers); otherwise stitching must use direct or fixed-term employees.
The principal employer must ensure welfare facilities and is liable to pay wages if the contractor defaults.

notes.note: The Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (along with the Trade Unions Act, 1926) has been replaced by the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, which retains the machinery of conciliation officers, Industrial Tribunals and the National Industrial Tribunal, and requires a Grievance Redressal Committee in establishments with 20 or more workers and a works committee in those with 100 or more. Strikes and lock-outs in any establishment now need 14 days' notice, given within 60 days before the strike, and are barred during conciliation and tribunal proceedings. Prior government permission for lay-off, retrenchment and closure is required for establishments with 300 or more workers (up from 100), retrenchment compensation is 15 days' average pay per completed year of service, and the employer must also contribute 15 days' wages to a worker reskilling fund.

The Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946 is now Chapter IV of the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, which applies to industrial establishments with 300 or more workers (up from 100). The employer may adopt the model standing orders framed by the Central Government on matters such as classification of workers, shift working, attendance, leave, termination, misconduct and grievance redressal, or prepare its own and get them certified by the certifying officer. Where the employer adopts the model standing orders, they are deemed certified, which saves time for a new establishment.

quiz.q: Workers of a company with 120 workers want to go on strike. Under the IR Code, 2020, what notice is required?
options: No notice; only public utilities need notice
At least 14 days' notice, given within 60 days before the strike
quiz.explain: The IR Code extends the 14-day strike notice requirement, previously limited to public utility services, to all industrial establishments.

quiz.q: A factory with 250 workers wants to retrench 30 workers. Does it need prior government permission?
options: Yes, if it has more than 100 workers
Only if the workers are unionised
No; prior permission is needed only for establishments with 300 or more workers
quiz.explain: Chapter X of the IR Code requires prior permission for lay-off, retrenchment and closure only in establishments with 300 or more workers.

quiz.q: A worker with 6 years and 8 months of continuous service is retrenched. Apart from notice, what retrenchment compensation is due?
options: 15 days' average pay for each completed year, plus 15 days' wages to the reskilling fund
quiz.explain: The IR Code requires 15 days' average pay per completed year (and any part over six months) plus a contribution to the reskilling fund.

quiz.q: A company has 150 workers. Does Chapter IV (standing orders) of the IR Code apply?
options: Yes, it applies to all establishments
Yes, to those with 100 or more workers
No, it applies only to establishments with 300 or more workers
quiz.explain: The IR Code raised the threshold for standing orders from 100 to 300 workers.

quiz.q: An establishment adopts the model standing orders notified by the Central Government. What is their status?
options: They must be certified within one year
They are deemed to be certified
They are valid only after tribunal approval
quiz.explain: Under the IR Code, model standing orders adopted by an employer are deemed certified.

quiz.q: Which committee must every establishment with 20 or more workers constitute under the IR Code?
quiz.explain: The IR Code requires a Grievance Redressal Committee in every industrial establishment with 20 or more workers.

desc.q: Alpha Engineering Ltd employs 320 workers. Owing to falling orders, it wants to retrench 40 workers and is facing a threatened strike by the union. Advise the management on the legal requirements under the applicable law.
points: Since the establishment has 300 or more workers, Chapter X of the Industrial Relations Code, 2020 (replacing the ID Act, 1947) requires prior permission of the appropriate government for retrenchment, with an application stating reasons.
It must give three months' notice or wages in lieu, pay retrenchment compensation of 15 days' average pay per completed year, and deposit 15 days' wages per worker in the reskilling fund.
It should follow last-come-first-go within the category unless reasons are recorded, and give retrenched workers preference in re-employment.
A strike is illegal unless the union gives 14 days' notice within 60 days before it, and is barred during conciliation and for seven days after its conclusion.
Management should engage through conciliation; illegal strikes or lock-outs attract penalties under the Code.

notes.note: The Payment of Wages Act, 1936 is now part of the Code on Wages, 2019, which applies wage-payment rules to all employees regardless of wage ceiling. Wages must be paid by the 7th day of the following month for monthly-rated employees (or at the end of the shift, week or fortnight for others), and within two working days when an employee is removed, dismissed, retrenched or resigns. Authorised deductions, such as for fines, absence, advances and taxes, cannot together exceed 50% of wages in a wage period. The Code's single definition of wages excludes allowances such as HRA and conveyance, but if such exclusions exceed 50% of total remuneration, the excess is added back to wages.

The Minimum Wages Act, 1948 has been replaced by the Code on Wages, 2019, which extends minimum wages to all employees in all employments instead of only scheduled employments. The Central Government fixes a floor wage, considering minimum living standards, and no state may set minimum wages below it; minimum wages are fixed by time or piece work based on skill, geographical area and arduousness and revised at intervals not exceeding five years. Normal working hours and overtime at twice the normal rate also apply.

The Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 is now part of the Code on Wages, 2019. Every employee earning up to the notified wage ceiling who has worked at least 30 days in the year is entitled to a minimum bonus of 8.33% of wages or ₹100, whichever is higher, and a maximum of 20% based on the allocable surplus, with set-on and set-off of surplus over the years. Bonus calculation uses the notified wage limit, and an employee dismissed for fraud, violent behaviour, theft or sabotage is disqualified.

The Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 has been replaced by the Code on Wages, 2019, which prohibits discrimination in wages and in recruitment and conditions of employment on the ground of gender (including transgender persons) for the same or similar work. 'Same or similar work' means work needing the same skill, effort, experience and responsibility under similar conditions. An employer cannot reduce anyone's wages to comply, so if women packers are paid less than men for the same job, their pay must be raised to the men's level.

quiz.q: A monthly-rated employee resigns on 10 March. By when must the employer pay his final wages under the Code on Wages, 2019?
options: Within 7 days of the next month
Within two working days of resignation
At the time of full and final settlement
quiz.explain: The Code on Wages requires wages to be paid within two working days of removal, dismissal, retrenchment or resignation.

quiz.q: An employee's wage is ₹20,000 and the employer wants to deduct ₹12,000 in one month towards an advance and fine. Is this lawful?
options: Yes, advances can be fully recovered
Yes, if done over one month
No, total deductions cannot exceed 50% of wages in a wage period
quiz.explain: Under the Code on Wages, total authorised deductions in a wage period cannot exceed 50% of wages.

quiz.q: A state notifies a minimum wage that is lower than the floor wage fixed by the Central Government. The notification is:
options: Not valid, as minimum wages cannot be below the floor wage
Valid, as wages are a state subject
quiz.explain: The Code on Wages requires state minimum wages not to be lower than the national floor wage.

quiz.q: An employee who worked 25 days in the accounting year claims bonus. Is he eligible?
options: Yes, minimum bonus is always payable
No, at least 30 working days in the year is required
Only if the company made a profit
quiz.explain: The Code on Wages requires at least 30 days of work in an accounting year for bonus eligibility.

quiz.q: An employee's total remuneration is ₹50,000, of which basic and DA are ₹20,000 and allowances excluded from wages are ₹30,000. What is 'wages' under the Code on Wages?
quiz.explain: Since exclusions (₹30,000) exceed 50% of remuneration (₹25,000), the excess ₹5,000 is added back, giving wages of ₹25,000.

quiz.q: A company pays transgender machine operators less than other operators doing the same work. This violates:
options: Nothing, since only men and women are protected
The Code on Wages, 2019's prohibition of gender discrimination in wages
quiz.explain: The Code on Wages prohibits discrimination on grounds of gender, which includes transgender persons, in wages for the same or similar work.

desc.q: Bright Textiles Ltd restructured salaries so that basic pay is 30% of total remuneration and the rest is allowances, pays wages on the 12th of each month, and has not paid bonus for two years claiming losses. Advise on compliance with the Code on Wages, 2019.
points: Under the uniform definition of wages, excluded allowances above 50% of total remuneration are added back, so wages for PF, gratuity and bonus purposes must be at least 50% of remuneration.
Monthly wages must be paid by the 7th of the following month; paying on the 12th is a violation.

Minimum bonus of 8.33% of wages (or ₹100, whichever is higher) is payable to eligible employees who worked at least 30 days, even in a loss year, subject to the notified wage ceiling and the Code's exclusions.
Bonus must be paid within eight months from the close of the accounting year unless extended.
Non-compliance is an offence; first-time offences punishable with fine may be compounded, and employees can claim arrears before the authority.

notes.note: The ESI Act, 1948 is now Chapter IV of the Code on Social Security, 2020, applying to establishments with 10 or more employees and, by notification, to hazardous establishments with even one employee. Employees within the notified wage ceiling get medical, sickness, maternity, disablement and dependants' benefits, funded by employer and employee contributions at rates notified by the government. An employer who covers its establishment voluntarily, or a plantation that opts in, can also be brought under the scheme.

The Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 is now Chapter III of the Code on Social Security, 2020, applying to establishments with 20 or more employees, and covering the Provident Fund, Employees' Pension Scheme and Deposit-Linked Insurance Scheme. Contributions are generally 12% of wages each from employer and employee (10% for specified establishments), calculated on the Code's uniform definition of wages. Once covered, an establishment stays covered even if employee strength later falls below 20.

The Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 is now Chapter VI of the Code on Social Security, 2020. A woman who has worked at least 80 days in the 12 months before delivery is entitled to 26 weeks' paid maternity leave for the first two children (12 weeks for the third and later), 12 weeks for adopting a child below three months or for a commissioning mother, and the option of work from home where the work allows. Establishments with 50 or more employees must provide a creche, and the employer cannot dismiss a woman during her maternity leave.

The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 is now Chapter V of the Code on Social Security, 2020, applying to establishments with 10 or more employees. Gratuity is payable at 15 days' wages for each completed year of service on termination after five years' continuous service, but the five-year condition does not apply on death or disablement, and fixed-term employees get gratuity pro rata even for less than five years. The ceiling is ₹20 lakh, and gratuity can be forfeited for termination due to riotous conduct, violence or an offence of moral turpitude.

The Apprentices Act, 1961 is not subsumed in the Labour Codes and continues to govern apprenticeship training; apprentices are excluded from the definitions of worker and employee under the Codes. Every establishment with 30 or more workers must engage apprentices in a band of 2.5% to 15% of its total strength, including contractual staff, under the Apprenticeship Rules, 1992, and the employer pays the prescribed minimum stipend, part of which can be reimbursed under the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme. The apprenticeship contract is registered on the apprenticeship portal, and the employer is not bound to offer employment at the end of training unless the contract provides otherwise.

The Codes replace multiple Act-wise registrations, registers and returns with a single electronic registration, prescribed electronic registers and consolidated returns filed online, building on the earlier Ease of Compliance to Maintain Registers under various Labour Laws Rules, 2017. EPF and ESI contributions are already paid through monthly electronic challan-cum-returns (ECR) on the EPFO and ESIC portals. For an employer, this means one annual return under the OSH and other Codes instead of separate returns under the Factories Act, CLRA and others.

quiz.q: An employee resigns after 4 years and 7 months of continuous service. Is gratuity payable under the Code on Social Security, 2020?
options: No, five years' continuous service is required (except for death, disablement or fixed-term employees)
quiz.explain: Chapter V of the Code requires five years' continuous service for gratuity except on death or disablement, and for fixed-term employees.

quiz.q: A fixed-term employee completes a 2-year contract. Is gratuity payable?
options: Yes, pro rata for the period of service
Only if the contract is renewed
quiz.explain: The Code on Social Security, 2020 grants pro-rata gratuity to fixed-term employees irrespective of five years' service.

quiz.q: A woman employee expecting her second child has worked 120 days in the preceding 12 months. How much paid maternity leave is she entitled to?
options: No leave as she has another child
quiz.explain: Under Chapter VI of the Code, 26 weeks' maternity benefit is available for the first two children if 80 days of work are completed.

quiz.q: An establishment had 25 employees when EPF applied; strength now drops to 17. Must EPF contributions continue?
options: Yes, coverage continues even if strength falls below 20
quiz.explain: Once an establishment is covered under the EPF provisions, it continues to be covered despite a reduction in employees below 20.

quiz.q: A company has 200 workers. How many apprentices must it engage at minimum under the Apprenticeship Rules?
quiz.explain: Establishments with 30 or more workers must engage apprentices between 2.5% and 15% of total strength, so the minimum is 5.

quiz.q: An establishment with 60 employees has no creche. Under the Code on Social Security, 2020, this is:
options: Lawful, as creches are only for factories
Lawful if fewer than 30 women are employed
Unlawful, since every establishment with 50 or more employees must provide a creche
quiz.explain: The Code requires every establishment with 50 or more employees to provide a creche facility.

desc.q: Zen Retail Pvt Ltd employs 45 staff, including 10 fixed-term employees and 12 women. One woman is expecting her first child, a fixed-term employee leaves after three years, and the company has never registered under EPF or ESI. Advise on its obligations under the Code on Social Security, 2020.
points: With 45 employees it is covered for EPF (20+) and ESI (10+) under Chapters III and IV of the Code, which replaced the EPF Act, 1952 and ESI Act, 1948; it must register electronically and pay arrears with damages and interest.
The expecting employee, if she has worked 80 days in the last 12 months, gets 26 weeks' paid maternity leave, cannot be dismissed during leave, and may be allowed work from home if feasible.
The fixed-term employee is entitled to pro-rata gratuity at 15 days' wages per completed year, though service is under five years.
A creche is not mandatory below 50 employees, but will become so if strength reaches 50.
Contributions are calculated on wages under the Code's uniform definition, and monthly ECR returns plus consolidated electronic returns must be filed.

notes.note: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, which gave statutory form to the Vishaka guidelines (1997), requires every employer with 10 or more employees to constitute an Internal Committee headed by a senior woman employee, with at least half its members women and one external member from an NGO or familiar with women's issues (section 4); a Local Committee in each district handles complaints from smaller workplaces or against the employer (section 6). A complaint must be filed in writing within three months of the incident, extendable by three more months (section 9), conciliation is possible at the woman's request without monetary settlement (section 10), and the inquiry must be completed within 90 days (section 11), with the employer acting on the recommendations within 60 days. During the inquiry the committee may recommend interim relief such as transfer or leave (section 12), the identity of parties is confidential (section 16), and the employer must run awareness programmes and include POSH data in its annual report. Failure to constitute the Internal Committee attracts a fine up to ₹50,000, which doubles for a repeat offence and can lead to cancellation of licence (section 26).

quiz.q: A company has 8 employees. A woman employee wants to complain of harassment by a colleague. Where should she file?
options: Local Committee constituted by the District Officer
quiz.explain: Section 6 provides for a Local Committee to receive complaints from workplaces with fewer than 10 employees.

quiz.q: An incident occurred on 1 January. The complainant files on 20 May citing trauma. Can the Internal Committee accept it?
options: No, the limit is strictly three months
Yes, the committee can extend the limit by up to three months for recorded reasons
quiz.explain: Section 9 allows the three-month limit to be extended by a further three months if circumstances prevented timely filing.

quiz.q: During conciliation, the respondent offers ₹2 lakh to settle the complaint. Can this be the basis of settlement?
options: No, monetary settlement cannot be the basis of conciliation
Yes, if the amount is paid to the committee
quiz.explain: Section 10 bars monetary settlement as the basis of conciliation.

quiz.q: Within how many days must the Internal Committee complete its inquiry?
quiz.explain: Section 11(4) requires the inquiry to be completed within 90 days.

quiz.q: An employer with 50 employees has not constituted an Internal Committee. The penalty for the first offence is:
quiz.explain: Section 26 prescribes a fine of up to ₹50,000 for failing to constitute the Internal Committee.

quiz.q: Which of the following must be a member of the Internal Committee?
options: An external member from an NGO or person familiar with women's issues
quiz.explain: Section 4(2) requires one member from an NGO or association committed to women's causes, or a person familiar with sexual harassment issues.

desc.q: A woman employee of an IT company with 300 employees complains that her team lead repeatedly made sexually coloured remarks during client visits outside office. The company says the incident is outside the 'workplace' and in any case it has not yet constituted an Internal Committee. Advise.
points: Under section 2(o) of the POSH Act, 2013, 'workplace' includes any place visited by an employee during or arising out of employment, including transport, so client visits are covered.
Sexually coloured remarks fall within the definition of sexual harassment in section 2(n).
The company must immediately constitute an Internal Committee under section 4; failure attracts a fine up to ₹50,000 under section 26, doubled for repeat offences.

The complaint must be filed within three months (extendable by three months); the IC must complete the inquiry within 90 days, may grant interim relief such as transfer, and the employer must act within 60 days of the report.
Confidentiality under section 16 must be maintained, and the employer must report the case in its annual report and directors' report.
